mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent earnings declines.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a strong supply-side response, which typically boosts economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic expansions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6%, it signals a monetary policy response to a weak labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as liquidity is injected into the economy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and retail sales (RSAFS) also decline by more than 5% YoY, it signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of declining HOUST and RSAFS does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is hiked by more than 50 basis points in a single meeting, it signals a rapid tightening cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to the surprise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS hikes > 50bps do not correlate with subsequent negative returns.
